portion_doctrine: Series 5 (segments 51-53) is a video transcript collection: (1) '32 Claude Code Hacks' - beginner to advanced power-user techniques organized by difficulty; (2) '7 Claude Skills That Run My Business' - portfolio of production skills built by creator; (3) '10 Amazing Claude Skills' from Ishan Sharma featuring skill-creator, hook-forge, humanizer, infographic-builder, decision-framer, expand-and-contract, caveman, and find-skills. Content is operational, skill-focused, repetition-heavy with boilerplate YouTube/GitHub navigation. Core payload: hacks (numbered 1-32), skill taxonomy, and trigger phrases.
operating_rules: Use /init on every project to generate cloud.md
Set up a status line to monitor context % and cost in real-time
Keep context small: don't dump entire codebase, give Claude only what it needs for the current task
Compact at 60% context usage; use /compact with preserve options (e.g., keep API decisions, keep schema)
Always start in plan mode (shift+tab), let Claude outline steps before executing
Treat Claude like a junior developer: ask problems not commands, let it reason through approach
Build self-checking into to-do lists: include verification steps (screenshot, test, check errors)
Don't wait for Claude to finish wrong path: hit escape, correct course, reprompt early
Challenge outputs aggressively; demand higher bar on second try; update skill/cloud.md with improvements
Exit early with /re to undo and roll back to previous conversation point
Use /hooks for notifications (e.g., alert when session finishes)
Use /loop for recurring tasks (e.g., every 5 min check deployment); lasts max 3 days, use desktop scheduled tasks for longer
Use /compact but keep specific things: explicitly name what to preserve
Set permissions carefully: explicitly allow safe commands, explicitly deny destructive ones (not dangerously skip permissions)
Use Haiku for sub-agents on simple/data-heavy tasks; keep Opus for main thread
Refresh cloud.md constantly with new patterns/gotchas/conventions discovered; keep it 150-200 lines max
Route cloud.md to separate files (style guides, business context, reference docs) to avoid token bloat in system prompt
Use API endpoints instead of MCP servers when you only need one specific tool (saves tokens)
Skills are folders with instructions - portable, reusable, survive model/tool changes
Skills are best for repetitive tasks; if you find yourself doing the same thing daily/weekly, build a skill
Use skill creator (anthropic official) to build skills via natural language; it asks clarifying questions then builds the .md file
Skills can be improved: select 'improve existing skill' in skill creator for best-practice optimization
Use skills consistently: they get smarter over time when you bake context into them
No SQL data analytics: connect CLI tools (BigQuery BQ) to Cloud Code, ask plain English questions, Claude translates to queries
Use ultrathink when Claude needs maximum thinking budget (32k tokens): architecture decisions, complex debugging, big refactors
Work trees enable parallel sessions on same project without overwrites: claude-worktree [feature-name]
Remote control sessions from phone/browser: code stays local, connection remote-only
Host on VPS for always-on sessions; SSH in when needed; control via Telegram anytime
Sub-agents run in parallel with fresh context but can't talk to each other; agent teams can talk + share task list + assign work
Context 7 MCP solves training cutoff problem: has version-specific live docs for React, Next.js, MongoDB, etc.

prompts: Treat Claude like a junior developer: ask problems not commands
Don't dump entire codebase into context
Make Claude ask questions continuously until 95% confident
Tell Claude to update itself (skill/cloud.md) when it improves output
gates: Context rot gate: use /context to diagnose bloat before it breaks session
Early exit gate: escape and reask on wrong path to avoid wasted tokens
Skill improvement gate: only export/commit skill after aggressive challenge + update
Token budget gate: Haiku for sub-agents data-heavy tasks, Opus for main strategic thread
Cloud.md bloat gate: keep under 200 lines or route to separate files
Permissions gate: explicitly allow/deny instead of dangerously skip permissions
MCP token gate: use direct API endpoints instead of full MCP server if only need one tool
Skill-building gate: only build skill if doing task daily/weekly (repetition test)
Video analysis gate: use watch-video skill (auto-extracts transcript + key frames)
Decision gate: use decision-framer for any 'should I' question (structured reasoning)
content_ideas: Cloud Code hacks organized by beginner/intermediate/pro difficulty tiers
Skill portfolio templates: daily-planner, newsletter-workflow, content-repurposing pipeline
Mental models for decisions: contrarian check, assumption surfacing, second-order effects detection
Token optimization playbook: Haiku for data tasks, Opus for strategy, skill reuse patterns
Cloud.md best practices: 150-200 line limit, routing pattern, refresh cadence
Parallel session workflows with git worktrees
AI writing humanization: patterns to strip, vocabulary cleanup, em-dash elimination
Content hook psychology: 10 angles (curiosity, loss-frame, contrast, specificity, controversy, pattern-interrupt, identity, social-proof, future-pace, direct)
contradictions: Use dangerously-skip-permissions (fast) vs. explicitly allow/deny (safer): doc says never use dangerously-skip, always use explicit allow/deny
Dump entire codebase for context vs. keep context small: hacks say keep small; skill-creator may ask for whole project context initially
Skills are static folders vs. skills are living documents: skills should be refreshed/improved constantly but shipped as .skill packages
MCP servers load all tools vs. use direct API endpoints for token savings: creates decision paralysis on which approach per use case
weird_gold: Caveman skill cuts token usage by 75% while preserving technical accuracy - ultra-compressed communication model
Karpathy guidelines (folder-with-instructions pattern) predates modern AI; will outlast any tool/model change - meta-stability insight
Decision-framer surfaces unknowns that would change your mind: flips decision from binary (A/B) to hypothesis-driven (what's unknown?)
Hook-forge's 10 psychological triggers are repeatable and psychological-angle-based, not topic-dependent: portable across domains
Expand-and-contract four-bucket system (Core/Nice-to-have/Maybe-later/Out) == scope management language that survives tool changes
Sub-agents + Haiku for cheap data-heavy work, main thread + Opus for strategy = tiered-thinking cost architecture
Watch-video skill extracts transcripts + key frames from any link (YouTube/Loom/URL) without leaving Claude: breaks video-locked content
GEO-AEO content optimization (structuring articles for AI search engine citations) is the new SEO moat
Skills installed locally .skill files; can be git-committed, team-shared instantly via GitHub clone + install loop
Decision skill runs three sub-agents (options structured, contrarian check, weighting) in parallel then synthesizes verdict: distributed decision-making
